correctness.rationale: For the abstract dimensionless ODE, eliminate the first nullcline on 0<x<α to obtain β=B_α(x). Its endpoint limits are +∞ and 0. For pq≤1 the derivative is strictly negative. Otherwise its sign can change only above (pq−1)^(−1/q), where its numerator factors into a positive factor times α−F(x). F diverges at both ends of its domain, decreases then increases about its unique minimum α_c, and is greater than x there, so its two roots for α>α_c lie in the domain of B_α. This gives the stated counts. The Jacobian trace is −2 and its determinant has the opposite sign to B_α′, giving the two attracting outer equilibria and the intervening saddle. At either ordinary fold, B_α″≠0; changing coordinates locally to (x,ẋ) shows a nonzero quadratic center-manifold term (the acceleration on ẋ=0 is a smooth nonzero factor times β−B_α(x)). Hence the zero-eigenvalue fold equilibrium is not asymptotically stable, consistent with the open interval. At the cusp only the claimed linear type is needed. α_c is the infimum of the rates admitting two stable equilibria, not an attained minimum; the precise scope in RESULT.md lines 36–45 is clear on this point. For ε=α−α_c>0, differentiate F′ at its minimum to get D>0, expand the exact factored derivative uniformly on the O(√ε) layer as K(ε−Ds²/2)+O(ε^(3/2)), and integrate. The endpoints are ±√(2ε/D)+O(ε) relative to x_c; the derivative remainder integrates to O(ε²) and replacing the endpoints by the leading ones costs no more. The fixed-x change gives the displayed shared slope; the two integrals give opposite (2/3)K√(2/D) terms. Setting p=q=2 yields D=6 and K=1. This is a replay of RESULT.md lines 49–89, for fixed exponents only. The inspected verification record reports 337 finite rational/numerical assertions; the supplied script was not executed and these assertions do not prove the asymptotic law.

Its set characterization does not give the local fold-width coefficient or its coordinate slope.

evidence: Canonical cusp controls explain the exponent but recovering the coefficient requires derivatives of the control map. The frozen calculation computes both the curvature of the fold abscissa relation at its minimum and the positive prefactor in the derivative of the physical-coordinate ordinate, and uses them jointly.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A comparable coefficient could be derived for the restricted prior cusp by tracking its parameter map. Neither that restricted statement nor the broader parameter-set classification mechanically gives the two constants for all fixed positive real exponents in the original coordinates without the model-specific fold computation.

evidence: The original Box 1 equations agree by variable and exponent relabeling. Li–Zhang impose one exponent equal to 1, and in canonical controls obtain fold values ±2(μ₁/3)^(3/2). Cahn–Mochrie analyze a symmetric specialization including exponent 2.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The canonical exponent is the same phenomenon but the coefficient is not invariant under control reparametrization. Equality of a canonical constant with one symmetric example does not identify the original-coordinate coefficient for unequal exponents.

originality.rationale: Pass concerns the explicit coordinate-dependent leading width and balance-line coefficients for all fixed positive p,q with pq>1. It does not credit the model, the bistability/cusp classification where already established, or the generic three-halves exponent. The full accessible broad Hill-switch preprint was consulted, improving on the frozen access note; it gives substantial parameter-set coverage but not the same full exponent range or local quantitative result.
residual_risks: A less directly indexed bifurcation calculation or a published parameter map for additional exponent ranges could contain an exact equivalent. The bounded comparisons do not certify priority. No statement about implementation or experimental rate tolerances was evaluated.

value.rationale: A fixed-coordinate width is a natural quantitative invariant of this established planar model: it answers how quickly the three-equilibrium region opens in the original coordinates, which a canonical cusp shape does not quantify. The explicit exponent-dependent prefactor and first-order center slope, across nonsymmetric as well as symmetric cases, are the useful content; the generic exponent and equilibrium counts alone would not support this assessment. The result is mathematical and not an experimental calibration or a practical engineering claim.
